parsed.explanation: Combined regime: sexuality statutes (ss146/148, up to 10 and 5 years) remain in force and were upheld in February 2024, with no SOGI anti-discrimination law and no recourse for speaking out. Trans-specific evidence is thin: a 2019 fraud charge against a cross-dressing teen after a transphobic assault, withdrawn without reason, and a 2018 attack condemned by the head of government. Violence is documented only in general terms, with no denominators. No entry, facility, care or minor-specific rules are sourced. Silence is not treated as safety. Structural signals (criminalisation, no recognition, no support infrastructure, hostile online threats) place this in High Risk, with the sexuality statute weighted as a secondary lever.

entry_documents.exposure: No visa, entry-screening or admission rule affecting LGBT travellers is sourced. Gender-marker rules for travel documents are not documented.
entry_documents.interaction: A trans visitor travelling with a partner who would be read as same-sex under local law could engage ss146/148 at any stage. No route to recognition exists for such a relationship.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented 2019 case: a cross-dressing teenager, after being assaulted, was charged with fraud for allegedly pretending to be a woman. The charge was withdrawn in May 2019 without reason. No enforcement data for ss146/148 or recent prosecutions is available.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: The prosecutor withdrew the charge, which is a limited mitigating outcome.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Police or prosecutorial action against gender presentation (fraud framing) can follow victimisation, so a visitor who reports an attack could be exposed.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facilities law or practice is sourced. No subnational variation is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Cannot be assessed from the record.

care_services.exposure: Healthcare, medication and HIV service provision beyond naming a regional HIV organisation for MSM are not covered. No trans-specific care access is documented.
care_services.protection: A regional HIV organisation is named as the main contact point for MSM.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking may bring a visitor into contact with systems that have no documented trans-specific protocol.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Criminal statutes frame same-sex conduct as an offence. A 2011 article by a same-sex couple drew murderous threats. A 2011 college scheme targeted lecturers with 'homosexual tendencies' accusations. The High Court upheld the ban in 2024.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The head of government condemned the 2018 attacks, called the homophobia unacceptable and called for open dialogue.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing is mixed: criminal law is hostile, while senior condemnation of violence is a partial counterweight. Judicial reinforcement of the ban in 2024 is current.

minors_guardians.exposure: No LGBT youth helpline or help centre exists. The 2019 teenager case shows a minor being charged after assault. Minor-specific facilities or custody rules are not sourced.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor accompanying a trans adult has no documented support route if an incident occurs. Guardians face the same criminal exposure if the relationship is read as same-sex.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Bias-motivated violence against LGBT people is documented in general terms by a 2023 HRO report. The 2018 attack on three cross-dressing young men is documented. No trans-specific violence rate with denominators is available.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No SOGI anti-discrimination or hate-crime protection is documented. The head of government condemned the 2018 attacks.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: With no recourse and no denominator, violence is documented as a pattern of individual incidents. The state's response is mixed.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No law protects against discrimination or harassment based on SOGI. No LGBT organisation operates in the country. Two men left because of the law and a 22-year-old won asylum abroad.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Regional civil-society condemnation and HRO reporting exist, but neither operates as traveller-facing remedy.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absent remedies mean any exposure a visitor encounters has no documented route to relief.

anchor_checks.comparison: The anchor has an operative state register that excludes trans visitors at entry, which is absent here. This case is higher because entry screening is not documented. It is similar in having no effective remedy and a structural hostile climate.

The anchor has undercover entrapment, filmed blackmail and vice enforcement against trans people. The present dossier documents only one fraud charge, which was withdrawn. Enforcement data is absent. This case is therefore somewhat higher, but the criminal statute and lack of recourse keep it in the same tier.

The anchor has documented selective scrutiny and ejections under municipal rules with some complaint routes. The present case has no documented everyday service denial and no remedy. It is therefore lower, because the criminal statute and absent protections carry more weight.

parsed.synthesis: The criminal statutes remain in force and were upheld in 2024. The only trans-specific state-linked act documented is a fraud charge against a teenager after an assault, which was withdrawn. Violence is documented as individual incidents without denominators, and no SOGI protection or recourse operates. Entry, facility and care rules are not documented. The thin record is extrapolated toward the risk implied by criminalisation, absent recognition and absent support infrastructure. The partial mitigations are senior condemnation of violence and the withdrawn charge. Overall the operative regime sits in the High Risk band.
